sections.h2: What is the way to contact Lee County's register?
sections.html:
The number is 919-718-4585. Lee County's register works out of an office on South Horner Boulevard in Sanford and keeps weekday hours, 8:00 in the morning until 5:00. An earlier daily recording cutoff of 4:30 has applied to every document since January 1, 2017.

Its stated mission is to maintain, protect and make accessible every recorded transaction and the vital records of the county. For a seller, the main job is real estate: the office records instruments that are properly notarized, most of which concern land in Lee County, and keeps the index that title examiners search.

Marriage licenses here are by appointment only. A seller who needs vital records for an estate sale can order certified copies online through the link the county posts on its Register of Deeds page.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Lee County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Lee County bills $26.00 for a deed that runs to 15 pages and $4.00 for each sheet over that, while a security instrument such as a deed of trust is $64.00 through 35 pages. The county's printed schedule cites G.S. 161-10, the statewide fee statute.

sections.h2: How is the excise tax handled in Lee County?
sections.html:
The schedule prints the state excise tax on real estate conveyances as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 up to $500. Under the statute the seller owes one dollar per $500 of value, counting any leftover part as a full unit, and pays the register first.

The county's sheet adds a note on where the money goes. One half stays with the county, and the other half, less a 2 percent handling fee, goes to the state. That fee split is the county's bookkeeping and does not change what the seller owes.

When you receive a settlement statement from the closing attorney, look for the excise line on the seller side next to the recording line. Ask the register's office if the amount does not match the sale price on your contract.

sections.h2: Which Lee County documents carry no recording charge?
sections.html:
Cancellations are free, which covers releasing an old deed of trust. A military discharge is also free to file, along with one certified copy of it.

Everything else follows the page-based fees. The following items commonly come up when a house in Lee County is sold:

  • The seller's deed to the buyer, priced by its length.
  • The buyer's deed of trust, if there is a loan, charged at the higher base.
  • A cancellation of the seller's old loan, recorded for no fee.
  • A plat, if a lot is being split, at $21.00 a sheet.

For a cash sale there is no new loan to record, so the register's bill is usually just the deed fee and the excise stamp, plus any copies you ask for.

sections.h2: Can I be told when something is recorded against my Lee County property?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's page promotes a free property notification service where a person registers a name and receives an email whenever a document with that name is filed in the Lee County office. The sign-up goes through a state-wide notification website linked from the county page.

This helps owners who are away from a house, who own an inherited property, or who rent a home out. A filing under your name that you did not expect is a red flag for fraud, and the email gives you a chance to call the office quickly.

Deeds and other documents can also be searched through the Sanford and Lee County deeds online portal that the county links. Use it to confirm a deed from your closing has appeared and to read the book and page of earlier deeds.

sections.h2: What records can a Lee County seller get from the register?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the register issues certified copies of recorded instruments, $5.00 for the opening page plus $2.00 per page after it. A comparing copy for certification costs $5.00. These help when a lender or buyer's attorney wants a stamped copy of an older deed, easement or plat.

Estate sales often need vital records too. Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records are $10.00 each in the schedule, and certified vital records can be ordered online through a link on the county page. The county noted that, as of January 1, 2024, it could not pull out-of-county birth certificates until further notice, so heirs holding a certificate from another county should ask before making the trip.

Other items on the schedule that touch a sale:

  • A certificate for removal of graves, $12.00 for page one then $3.00 a page after that, which may come up when rural land with an old family plot is conveyed.
  • Right-of-way plans, $21.00 up front and $5.00 for every one after.
  • A UCC search for filings made before July 1, 2001, $38.00 per name plus $1.00 per copy.

sections.h2: Who handles a tax bill on a house in Lee County?
sections.html:
Property tax is handled separately from the register. The Lee County Tax Office, 106 Hillcrest Drive in Sanford, handles listing, appraisal and assessment of real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles, and it collects both current and delinquent taxes. It keeps weekday hours from eight to five.

Three direct lines cover the main needs:

  • Collections: 919-718-4662
  • Listings: 919-718-4661
  • Appraisals: 919-718-4660

The department offers a comparable sales tool called Comper on its page, which sellers can use to see recorded sales near their address. State rules apply to the bill itself: the bill falls due on September 1 and carries no interest if paid ahead of January 6, with 2 percent interest added after that date and 3/4 percent a month from February 1.

sections.h2: How big is the Lee County housing market?
sections.html:
Lee County's population is put at 70,258 in the Census count dated July 1, 2025, which is 11.0 percent above the 63,283 base from April 2020. Its 28,511 housing units share 255.06 square miles, a compact footprint by North Carolina standards.

Over 2020 to 2024 a typical owned home was worth $240,200, and owners lived in 67.3 percent of the housing stock, which leaves about a third rented at a median $1,017. Median household income came to $65,387, and workers averaged 25.8 minutes to get to a job.

Residents who identify as Hispanic or Latino are 23.7 percent of the county, and 20.6 percent of people age 5 and over use another language at home.

Permits were active in 2025 at 674, so new homes are part of the local supply. A resale usually competes with those new homes on price and move-in readiness.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Lee County house quickly and as is?
sections.html:
A direct cash sale skips the listing and the repair list, but it still ends at this same register's office. The seller signs the deed, the closing agent presents it before the 4:30 p.m. cutoff, and the seller's excise tax is paid before the register records it.

Before saying yes to an offer, collect your own deed, a loan payoff statement if you owe on the house, and the newest tax bill. If a lien shows on the title, ask the lender to record its cancellation so the record is clear for the next owner.

faqs.q: What time does the Lee County Register of Deeds stop recording documents?
faqs.a: 4:30 p.m. daily. Weekday service continues until five, though since January 1, 2017 the office has stopped recording documents half an hour earlier.

faqs.q: What will a Lee County deed cost at the register's counter?
faqs.a: A deed is $26.00 through 15 pages, with $4.00 added per further page. Mortgage paperwork is $64.00 through 35 pages. The excise stamp comes on top of either.

faqs.q: Does Lee County charge to cancel a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The Lee County fee schedule lists cancellations at no fee, so recording a release of an old loan does not add to the seller's costs.

faqs.q: Who is charged the transfer stamp on a Lee County deed?
faqs.a: The seller does. The transferor settles it with the register before recording, at one dollar per $500 of price, with any remainder counted as another unit.

faqs.q: Is there a free alert for new filings under my name in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers a free property notification service that emails you when a document with your registered name is filed in the Lee County office.
